pairing: Same tasks, seeds, agent seeds (1000*seed + 14400 + slot), judge seeds; slots 8-11 exist only in D12. Run-to-run noise (~4 cases per 96) applies to paired solved counts.
judge: thinking judge with one-sentence reason (run_variants.judge_with_reason), unchanged; the exact verifier only scores
concurrency_note: At most 4 agents in flight per case in every arm, 20 cases at once, per-endpoint slot cap 20 (agents and judges) <= 25. Escalation agents run on the node of the agent they replace.
runner: run_variants.py --policy ARM, one arm at a time, driven by inkling/arms.py
execution: Arms run sequentially in arm_order, each alone on the fleet via inkling/arms.py (fresh admission with the shim sha and mem fraction below, prefix-cache flush, server counters, idle wait, GPU energy). Watchdog inkling/watch.sh; MemAvailable logged every 60 s.
resume_rule: If an arm stops on an infrastructure fault (runner stop flag, worker or judge infra failure, node fault), the fault is fixed and the same arm is continued with arms.py --resume-from (skips its cases that finished without infra faults; reruns the others with the same seeds) and documented as an amendment. Server tokens, wall and energy of an arm are then the sums over its segments (wasted work of the stopped segment included and reported separately). Never a silent restart; no case is dropped.
exclusions: None. All 96 cases of each arm count.
generator: make_arithmetic_hard.py --seed 2026112110 --protocol arithmetic-hard-v14 --output datasets/arithmetic-hard-v14 (after this plan is committed and pushed); same rules as hard-v5..v13

serving.launch: inkling/serve.sh, MEM=0.75 since 2026-11-21 16:25 Europe/Warsaw (KV ~1.08M tokens per node)
serving.adapter: inkling/shim.py (vLLM dialect; client disconnects close the upstream stream and count as shim:client_cancels)

frozen_note: Frozen 2026-11-22 BEFORE arithmetic-hard-v14 exists. Replication of swarm-cap12-hard12-v1, where failure-driven escalation to 12 agents (roll12strategy) solved 85/96 vs 81/96 for the default (roll8strategy), paired +6/-2, 0 wrong, 2 cases answered only by agents 9-12, at +24 % tokens and +29 % wall. The owner's priority is quality: cap 12 becomes the default if the gain repeats with 0 wrong answers.
question: On a second fresh corpus, does cap 12 again solve more cases than cap 8 with 0 wrong answers?

arms.D: roll8strategy (default): 4 in flight; failures replaced by fresh-seed agents with strategy hints, up to 8; first accept cancels the rest
arms.D12: roll12strategy: identical, cap 12 agents (escalation still strictly failure-driven; no time trigger)

primary_outcomes.replication: hard-v14: D12 solved vs D solved, paired two-sided exact sign test; wrong answers; late rescues (answered by slots 8-11).
primary_outcomes.pooled: Pre-registered pooled test over hard-v12 + hard-v14 (192 paired cases): D12 vs D, two-sided exact sign test.
primary_outcomes.cost: Server tokens per case, arm wall, GPU energy per solved case, D12 vs D (reported, not gates).

decision_rule: roll12strategy (cap 12) becomes the default if: 0 wrong answers on hard-v14 AND D12 solved >= D solved + 2 on hard-v14 AND late rescues >= 1 on hard-v14. The pooled hard-v12 + v14 sign test is reported as the strength of evidence. Cost is reported but is not a gate (owner priority: quality). Otherwise cap 12 stays the max-accuracy mode and cap 8 the default.
secondary_outcomes: GPU energy per solved case; escalated cases and agents; answering-slot histogram; judge verdicts and false accepts.
baseline_note: Defaults: arithmetic roll8strategy (4 in flight; 3 in flight was worse in swarm-width3-hard11-v1); coding early stop + staggered start.
smoke: Same code as swarm-cap12-hard12-v1 (roll12strategy smoke-tested there); no new code.
